title: U.S. House · Colorado's 1st District

context.text: This is an open seat: Melat Kiros defeated incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette and Wanda James 53.2%-39.8%-7.0% in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary, so DeGette will not appear on the November ballot. Christy Peterson advanced unopposed from the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Melat Kiros
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette

priorities.text: Campaign finance and lobbying reform, plus congressional term limits, to reduce the influence of money in politics.
Expanding voting rights and consolidating elections into a single day with a shorter election cycle.
Codifying access to housing, health care, nutritious food and public education as basic needs for every American.

positions.summary: Campaign website says she will always stand for Medicare for All and describes health care access as directly linked to life expectancy and economic outcomes.
Says she will always stand for universal childcare as part of putting working families first.
Campaign website calls for an arms embargo, saying U.S. tax dollars have funded what she describes as a genocide in Palestine.

priorities.text: Public safety: says reducing crime and 'soft on crime' policies in Denver is her top priority, arguing this would let businesses and visitors return to the city.
Reducing government waste, fraud and abuse, and creating incentives for business growth and job creation.

positions.summary: Lists the Save America Act among the measures she supports in her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
positions.quote: Yes to election integrity, the Save America Act, paper ballots, same day voting & hand count.

candidates.name: Chad Humphrey

priorities.text: Lists his three key campaign messages as restoring the Constitution, ending the Federal Reserve and the IRS, and stopping what he calls endless wars.
Says he is personally passionate about free markets.

candidates.researchNotes: Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, which did not directly address any of the guide's tracked issue statements; no separate campaign website was found.

candidates.name: Shimon Blau

priorities.text: Says he is running as an independent who rejects contributions from PACs and special-interest groups, saying he answers only to the people of the district.

Says he would caucus with Democrats and support Rep. Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker as a check on the Trump administration, while remaining willing to oppose Democratic-backed policies he disagrees with.
Wants to strengthen Denver's local economy by supporting small businesses, encouraging investment, and improving public safety.

positions.summary: In a Colorado Politics voter guide he says criminal aliens who threaten public safety should be deported, and also calls for fast-tracking legal status for long-term residents and for training and accountability for immigration agents.
positions.quote: Criminal aliens who threaten public safety should be deported, and our streets must be safer. At the same time, we should fast-track legal status for long-term, contributing members of our communities who have built their lives here.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response found; background and positions are drawn from his campaign website (blauforcongress.com), which does not have a dedicated issues page but discusses his priorities on the home page.

statements.quote: I support a woman's right to make her own healthcare decisions
statements.context: On his campaign website; the page does not use the word abortion

candidates.name: Critter Milton

priorities.text: In his most recent completed Ballotpedia survey (2022), listed his three key campaign messages simply as 'Unity, Unity, Unity.'
In an earlier (2020) survey, said his priorities included free universal education using technology, action on climate change, and ending prohibition by legalizing currently banned substances.

candidates.researchNotes: Milton has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his most recent completed survey was in 2022 (for a different U.S. House race), so priorities above are dated and not necessarily current for this 2026 campaign. No campaign website with current issue positions was found.

researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script (not applicable to non-incumbents in this open-seat race). Chad Humphrey completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; Shimon Blau has an active campaign website with priorities and one clear issue position; Critter Milton's Ballotpedia biography and most recent completed survey (2022, for a different race) provide some background, though he has not completed a 2026 survey. Write-in candidates from the primary (StClair, Wren, Replin) are omitted as not having active general-election campaigns. Biography gaps: Christy Peterson's campaign did not respond to press requests and has a minimal website; Chad Humphrey and Critter Milton have only Ballotpedia survey-based biographical information.
